dataset_meta.update_note: Second verification pass. Two corrections from the first compile: (1) removed 'Alberta Indigenous Agricultural Funding' -- it was not a real standalone program, the $150K/$300K figures were RALP's own Indigenous-applicant tier, mistakenly split into a separate entry. (2) replaced 'Alberta Young Farmer Grants' ($75,000 grant, single-sourced from a secondary blog with no primary confirmation found) with AFSC's real Next Generation Loan program -- a loan with a preferential interest rate, not a non-repayable grant. Four other entries had generic/imprecise source_urls corrected to specific program pages, and Women in Ag Grant moved from secondary-source-only to fully verified against a primary source.
dataset_meta.note: All figures verified against official Alberta.ca / AFSC / RDAR sources. Programs change frequently -- treat 'last_verified' as a freshness field the crawler should overwrite, not a permanent value.

programs.name: Next Generation Loan
programs.type: loan -- repayable financing with a preferential interest rate, NOT a non-repayable grant

funding_amount.structure: Fixed-rate term loan; eligible borrowers under 40 get a 1% interest rate reduction for the first 5-year term on up to $1,500,000 in lifetime principal

programs.eligible_use: Establishing or expanding a farming operation -- land, equipment, and other capital assets

eligibility.applicant_type: New, young (under 40), or returning agricultural producers; over-40 applicants may qualify if farm income was under $10,000 for 3 of the last 5 years
eligibility.ownership_requirement: 20% Next Generation borrower ownership required for joint/corporate applications

required_documents: Financial and business plan documentation per standard AFSC lending requirements
programs.correction_note: This entry replaces a previous 'Alberta Young Farmer Grants' entry describing a $75,000 non-repayable grant. That figure could not be verified against any primary source and appears to have been inaccurate -- this is the real program serving the same audience, correctly characterized as a loan.
